channel.title: Malcolm X — Archival Audio
channel.description: Personal listening index of original Malcolm X speech recordings, one continuous MP3 per speech. Audio linked from third-party archives; not affiliated with the sources.
channel.itunes:author: Malcolm X (archival audio)

item.title: On Afro-American History — OAAU Rally (1965)
item.description: Original Malcolm X archival audio. Recording date: 1965-01-24. OAAU address on recovering Black history, challenging colonial narratives, and connecting historical knowledge with liberation. One continuous MP3; no separate parts. Archival recording quality varies.

item.title: Prospects for Freedom in 1965 — Militant Labor Forum
item.description: Original Malcolm X archival audio. Recording date: 1965-01-07. Extended Militant Labor Forum recording on independent Black political action, the Congo, and international liberation struggles. One continuous recording, approximately 75 minutes. One continuous MP3; no separate parts. Archival recording quality varies.

item.title: To Mississippi Youth — SNCC Civil Rights Workers (1964–65)
item.description: Original Malcolm X archival audio. Recording date: 1965-01-01. Address to visiting Mississippi civil rights workers, encouraging independent thought and resistance. Sources date the occasion December 31, 1964 or January 1, 1965; this file is labeled January 1. One continuous MP3; no separate parts. Archival recording quality varies.

item.title: The Afro-American Problem as a World Problem — OAAU Rally (1964)
item.description: Original Malcolm X archival audio. Recording date: 1964-12-13. Extended Audubon Ballroom rally recording associated with Abdulrahman Mohamed Babu and Dick Gregory. Includes the rally context; not the June 1964 founding rally or February 1965 Rochester speech. One continuous MP3; no separate parts. Archival recording quality varies.

item.title: HARYOU-ACT Forum — Harlem Youth (1964)
item.description: Original Malcolm X archival audio. Recording date: 1964-12-12. Address to Harlem Youth Opportunities Unlimited–Associated Community Teams, on the conditions facing Black youth and the wider freedom struggle. One continuous MP3; no separate parts. Archival recording quality varies.

item.title: The Harlem Hate-Gang Scare — Militant Labor Forum and Discussion (1964)
item.description: Original Malcolm X archival audio. Recording date: 1964-05-29. Extended Militant Labor Forum recording associated with The Harlem Hate-Gang Scare and subsequent discussion. Runs 64:56; longer than the commonly isolated 18-minute address. One continuous MP3; no separate parts. Archival recording quality varies.

item.title: Return from Mecca — Press Conference (1964)
item.description: Original Malcolm X archival audio. Recording date: 1964-05-21. Press conference following his pilgrimage, documenting his changing views on race, religion, and international solidarity. Labeled as a press conference rather than a formal speech. One continuous MP3; no separate parts. Archival recording quality varies.

item.title: The Black Revolution — Militant Labor Forum (1964)
item.description: Original Malcolm X archival audio. Recording date: 1964-04-08. Post-split address connecting Black liberation in America with anticolonial revolutions abroad. Distinct from the 1963 Abyssinian Baptist Church address. This archive copy runs 45:13; editions with additional discussion can run longer. One continuous MP3; no separate parts. Archival recording quality varies.

item.title: A Declaration of Independence (1964)
item.description: Original Malcolm X archival audio. Recording date: 1964-03-12. Short press statement explaining his independent course after leaving the Nation of Islam, including political action and self-defense. A standalone statement, not an excerpt from a longer speech. One continuous MP3; no separate parts. Archival recording quality varies.

item.title: God’s Solution to America’s Race Problem — Ford Hall Forum (1963)
item.description: Original Malcolm X archival audio. Recording date: 1963-10. Ford Hall Forum address. Suffolk University’s forum archive dates the lecture October 6, 1963; the audio filename says October 10. The precise date is therefore qualified here. One continuous MP3; no separate parts. Archival recording quality varies.

item.title: The Black Revolution — Abyssinian Baptist Church (1963)
item.description: Original Malcolm X archival audio. Recording date: 1963-06. The earlier Black Revolution address at Abyssinian Baptist Church, distinct from the April 1964 Militant Labor Forum speech. The archive catalogs it in June 1963. One continuous MP3; no separate parts. Archival recording quality varies.

item.title: The Race Problem in America — Michigan State, with Press Conference and Q&A (1963)
item.description: Original Malcolm X archival audio. Recording date: 1963-01-23. Michigan State University’s archival recording: press conference and interview takes, followed by the university address and audience questions. Original university-hosted MP3; 65:06. One continuous MP3; no separate parts. Archival recording quality varies.

item.title: The Black Man’s History (1962)
item.description: Original Malcolm X archival audio. Recording date: 1962-12. Extended early-period lecture presenting Malcolm X’s Nation of Islam-era account of Black history. Included to document his earlier ideas alongside his later speeches. One continuous MP3; no separate parts. Archival recording quality varies.

item.title: Who Taught You to Hate Yourself? — Ronald Stokes Memorial (1962)
item.description: Original Malcolm X archival audio. Recording date: 1962-05-05. Extended memorial address on police violence and Black self-respect, beyond the familiar short excerpt. UCLA dates the memorial to May 5, 1962; the audio filename incorrectly says April 28. One continuous MP3; no separate parts. Archival recording quality varies.

item.title: At the Embassy in Los Angeles (1961)
item.description: Original Malcolm X archival audio. Recording date: 1961-04. Early Nation of Islam period address. The source dates this April 16, 1961; other catalogs differ. This copy runs 77:39. One continuous MP3; no separate parts. Archival recording quality varies.

item.title: After the Firebombing — Ford Auditorium (1965)
item.description: Original Malcolm X archival audio. Speech date: 1965-02-14. Ford Auditorium, Detroit, Michigan. Sometimes circulated as The Last Speech; Malcolm X spoke again after this date. One continuous recording (1:25:12); no separate parts. Hosted by Internet Archive. Archival tape quality varies.

item.title: With Fannie Lou Hamer — Mississippi Freedom Democratic Party Rally (1964)
item.description: Original Malcolm X archival audio. Speech date: 1964-12-20. Williams Institutional CME Church, Harlem. The source filename says December 24; the rally is documented as December 20 by archival sources. One continuous recording (26:18); no separate parts. Hosted by Internet Archive. Archival tape quality varies.

item.title: The African Revolution and Its Impact on the American Negro — Harvard (1964)
item.description: Original Malcolm X archival audio. Speech date: 1964-12-16. Harvard Law School Forum, including discussion. One continuous recording (51:37); no separate parts. Hosted by Internet Archive. Archival tape quality varies.

item.title: Oxford Union Debate (1964)
item.description: Original Malcolm X archival audio. Speech date: 1964-12-03. Malcolm X’s address and interventions at the Oxford Union; this is his contribution, not the entire evening of other speakers. One continuous recording (33:48); no separate parts. Hosted by Internet Archive. Archival tape quality varies.

item.title: The Ballot or the Bullet (1964)
item.description: Original Malcolm X archival audio. Speech date: 1964. Single continuous archival recording. The source filename dates it April 4, 1964; that date is not independently established. One continuous recording (53:10); no separate parts. Hosted by Internet Archive. Archival tape quality varies.

item.title: Message to the Grassroots (1963)
item.description: Original Malcolm X archival audio. Speech date: 1963-11-10. King Solomon Baptist Church, Detroit, Michigan. One continuous recording (46:37); no separate parts. Hosted by Internet Archive. Archival tape quality varies.

item.title: Racial Separation — University of California, Berkeley (1963)
item.description: Original Malcolm X archival audio. Speech date: 1963-10-11. University of California, Berkeley. One continuous recording (40:08); no separate parts. Hosted by Internet Archive. Archival tape quality varies.

item.title: Harlem Unity Rally (1963)
item.description: Original Malcolm X archival audio. Speech date: 1963-08-10. Harlem, New York City. One continuous recording (1:57:44); no separate parts. Hosted by Internet Archive. Archival tape quality varies.
